answer: Each agent’s actions can be gated by a privacy-preserving proof of a scarce, costly resource, such as a small deposit locked for a fixed period. The protocol accepts only one active identity per proof and slashes deposits when identities coordinate to manipulate rewards. A cipher can hide the owner while still verifying the proof; reaching the zenith of influence therefore requires many independently funded deposits, not merely many usernames. A pearl of reputation earned by one identity cannot be copied to the rest, so a sybil attacker must tie up real capital and risk losing it.
